_description: The model version identifier (IP-unified-architecture §10). MAJOR = structural change (a law, a divisor set, H). MINOR = refit (coefficients move, structure does not). Deliberately OUTSIDE model-parameters.json: a version label must not change the model's content identity (CONSTANTS_HASH). Seeded at v10.0 continuing the repo's existing v9/v10 tag lineage (owner decision); MAJOR/MINOR bumps proceed from here under this scheme. Content identity is carried separately by CONSTANTS_HASH (model parameters) and COEFFICIENTS_HASH (the fit) in packages/physics/src/constants/.
_v20Note:
v19.0 → v20.0 (plan 07, the windowAffine bound): a structural MAJOR — the planet chain's evaluation form beyond its fit window changes. The K4.5 periodic layer's era affine (windowAffine: off + slope·dt on the mean longitude, the semi-major axis and the k/h, q/p vectors — the anchor-snapshot-vs-window-content term the k45e era solve fits over ±2,500 yr) was the chain's one UNBOUNDED term: a fitted linear slope extrapolated to deep time, against the no-polynomial rule. The evaluator now holds the slope's argument at the fit-window edge (a hard clamp at ±meta.periodicTermsSpanYr, carried onto every chain by buildPlanetChainsFromArtifactData; a windowAffine without its span is refused), so inside the window nothing moves — the era goldens, the chain core, chain-vs-JPL (108,443 samples), the Earth channel and every campaign artifact reproduce with identical values — and beyond it the multi-mode secular skeleton carries the chain alone. MEASURED: unclamped, the slope alone had moved Saturn's mean longitude 430°, Neptune's semi-major axis 1,342 ppm and Mercury's orbit normal ~2° by ±100 kyr. The D5 handover boundaries (where the chain departs the banked series by |Δz| > 0.005 or 0.25° of orbit normal) move from Mercury 26/20, Venus 28/32, Mars 18/16, Jupiter 138/86, Saturn 222/88, Uranus 84/36, Neptune 134/358 kyr (past/future) to 12/18, 80/150, 16/16, 1344/854, 442/604, 72/76, 432/432 — the giants' boundaries were the affine's extrapolation, not the skeleton's; Mercury's past side shortens because the slope had been carrying secular curvature the mode sum lacks there, which is now the series' job sooner (global minimum 16 → 12 kyr). The deep-time planet positions at ±100 kyr move accordingly (42 Node golden rows, the browser's scenePlanet rows at the same epochs). The series verdict now hashes the evaluator and the chain artifact its handover rows run on. Hashes unchanged (no constant or coefficient moved). REGISTRY: 21 published keys move — the planets' inclination statistics over the banked ±10-Myr series (

InclMean/InclAmp/InclMin/InclMax; the chain is read out to its boundary, the series beyond), which the unbounded affine had inflated inside the old boundaries — Saturn's half-range 0.2736 → 0.1259° (max 1.16 → 1.02°), Neptune's 0.2018 → 0.1808°, Jupiter's 0.1379 → 0.1440°, the means at the 1e-4° level; and the Uranus/Neptune FluctuationMin/Max rows (Neptune +881/−791 → +895/−801). @essrt/physics MAJOR 16 (the evaluator contract), @essrt/model-values 14.1.0 (values move, no key leaves).

The retired laws' inputs are deleted from model-parameters.json: the per-planet H·num/den perihelion fractions (perihelionEclipticFraction; Mercury 8H/11 = 243,867 yr), the divisor table (fibonacciD), the ψ phase anchors (inclinationCycleAnchor) and the anti-phase flag (antiPhase), for the seven planets and the four additional bodies. perihelionEclipticYears is now the N-body chain's inertial apsidal period in every runtime, 1,296,000/g yr from the governed artifact (the value the API and the registry already published; Mercury 232,437 yr), with no deep-time H-scaling (g scales with the solar mass only). The constants hash moves (the JSON is embedded wholesale); the coefficients hash does not. @essrt/physics MAJOR 15 (the constants type loses the four fields), @essrt/model-values MAJOR 14 (the seven

InclCycleAnchor keys leave). check-literals now FAILS if any of the four keys returns. docs/retired-record.md is the record.
_v18Note: v17.0 → v18.0 (plan 07 R5/R9): a structural MAJOR — a second LAW retires. The ψ inclination law is deleted: ψ = 3·A_earth·√(m_E/m_☉) inverted from Earth's calibration, the per-planet amplitude ψ/(d·√m) with the mean from the J2000 constraint, and the device built on it — the ICRF-perihelion-linked inclination oscillation, the linear year-2000 node, the asc-node integrator dΩ/dε = −sin Ω / tan i, the two-normal ecliptic inclination — across the package (@essrt/physics MAJOR 14: planets/fibonacci-laws, planets/orientation, planets/asc-node-integrator removed), the Node engine, the browser and the Python bridge. Earth's H/3 inclination cosine and −H/5 linear node (the K device's Earth half) go with it: model.earth.inclinationDeg / ascendingNodeDeg are now the ONE-SOURCE engine Earth-orbit normal against the banked invariable plane (≡ the simulator's inclInvPlaneModel / ascNodeInvPlaneModel; device vs one-source 1.578677° vs 1.578422° at J2000, 1.24° vs 1.91° at −100 kyr). A planet's inclination and node of date have one home, the N-body chain. The K device constants (earthtiltMean, earthInvPlaneInclinationAmplitude, earthRAAngle, earthInvPlaneInclinationMean) stay as the scene's J2000 pose inputs. Hashes unchanged (no coefficient moved); docs/retired-record.md is the record.
_v17Note: v16.2 → v17.0 (plan 07 R6): a structural MAJOR — a LAW retires. The K eccentricity law is deleted: K inverted from Earth's calibration (K = e_amp·√m·a^1.5/(sin ε·√d)) and the System-Reset construction it fed (base = A·cos θ + √(e_J2000² − A²sin²θ) at the J2000 phase, θ on the wobble beat with a 90°/270° anti-phase offset). A planet's eccentricity of date now has ONE home, the N-body chain. Same class as v13.0, which retired the Fibonacci structural CLAIMS; this retires the machinery behind the eccentricity half of them. THE PHYSICS NUMBERS ARE UNCHANGED: four campaign artifacts regenerated with zero changed values (eclipse-audit 244/256 identified χ² 50.6, sun-vs-horizons 24,001 cardinal instants mean −0.71 min sd 0.94 min, chain-vs-jpl-rms 108,443 samples, lunar-alignment — the last two REFUSE on divergence, so a clean write is positive evidence), the cross-twin identity gate bit-exact at 103 values and still fail-proven, and the full chain plus the browser tier green with cross-engine parity on every shared probe. Measured first (plan 07 §9e): scaling the law's outputs by 1.10 moved no scene position and no published record field. WHAT WENT WITH IT: 60 consumer-less registry keys; the seven planet wobble centres (rendered markers whose radius and phase were the law's — no chain quantity replaces them like for like, the dominant eccentricity-vector mode being 24× to 38,950× larger); the planets' equation-of-centre path in both twins; pipeline steps 7a/7b; nineteen instruments — ten JS (verify-laws, balance-search, config1-proof, configuration-analysis, dual-balance-optimizer, eccentricity-balance, epoch-independence, inclination-verification, inclination-optimization, balance-with-dynamical-nodes) and thirteen Python (the balance suite, the Law-4 tilt prediction, the Planet-Nine screening), tools/verify/ 33 → 24 scripts. DELIBERATE MOVEMENT: the scene ellipse geometry now reads the OBSERVED J2000 eccentricity where it read the law's base (Mercury 6.9e-5 relative, Venus 1.21e-1, Mars perihelion distance −1.5 %) — wheel geometry, dead for positions, and the Node and browser goldens moved by identical ratios. FROZEN AS RECORD, not deleted: data/balance-presets.json, data/significance-results.json, data/mass-uncertainty-mc.json and the registry key kValue (3.4143e-6, labelled retired and no longer derived). Also fixed here: tools/lib/python/constants_scripts.py had been UNIMPORTABLE since v14.0's Phase 7 commit 2 retired the planets' obliquityCycle — KeyError on import, so every Python analysis had been unrunnable for months with nothing reporting it, because no gate runs them. Packages: @essrt/physics 13.0.0, @essrt/model-values 12.0.0.
_v16_2Note: v16.1 → v16.2 (2026-10, the running-mean dump): a MINOR — the same physics, a cleaner bank. The 20-Myr N-body dump records each 20,000-d sample as the RUNNING MEAN of the osculating vectors over its own interval (lattice-long-window-test.mjs mean=1, accumulated every 20 d) instead of the instantaneous elements: point sampling at 54.76 yr aliased ~1e-4 of Jupiter/Venus short-period content into the secular band (Earth's secular e read 0.5e-5 rms below DE441 through the series' 1-kyr boxcar — the Sun's 5″ annual line at −3500 — and the alias is not removable by any boxcar of such points). Re-banked on it: the deep secular mode table (frequencies unchanged to 1e-7, amplitudes at the 1e-5 level; the strongest Earth beat 405.6 kyr), the secular series (its node grid now anchored on multiples of 2000 yr INSIDE the raw span, so J2000, the ±50-kyr 1-kyr nodes and the λ̇ anchor fall on nodes exactly and no node sits in the boxcar's one-sided edge zone; the series spans ±9,996,000 yr and the consumers hand over to the mode tail beyond its last node as before), the obliquity verdict, the sidereal-year channel, the Sun completion's embedded carriers and e-vectors with the long-period rows re-derived on them (composed J2000 amplitude 6.87″, window-independent; the Venus–Earth row 1.4825/0.9435), and the 1-Myr frequency artifact re-stamped with the Laskar et al. 2011 Table 6 reference labels. MEASURED: Earth's secular e vs DE441 through the series' boxcar 0.49 → 0.10e-5 rms (ϖ 56 → 8″); the dump vs La2004 3.0 → 2.4e-5 rms over the last 500 kyr; the Sun vs Horizons over ±3000 yr mean 2.49 → 1.74″, sd 3.32 → 2.06″ (−3000…−2000: 1.84 → 0.17″, the modern window unchanged at 0.84″); the equinox at −3000 vs Vondrák −6.59 → −5.84″. The anomalistic year (owner-found): the hybrid's e-vector is now interpolated in POLAR form (e and the unwrapped ϖ; the J2000 anchor joined as an (e, ϖ) offset) — differentiating cubic-interpolated Cartesian components biased the apsidal rate −0.003 ″/yr at every epoch ((ϖ̇·Δt)² and ë·Δt² terms at the 500-yr node spacing); the published J2000 apsidal rate is now the series' own slope, 11.609 ″/yr (apsidal period 111,634 yr, anomalistic year 31,558,432.46 s; the point-sampled series read 11.615 by its alias, the textbook mean element is 11.612 — a labelled theory-vs-theory gap of 0.003 ″/yr, 0.07 s, not a tuning target). The deep-time Moon's arguments at +100/+277 kyr move 17–28° (the Earth e-vector slope anchor −8.21997e-7 → −8.22037e-7 /yr integrated through the lunar chain's eccentricity channel — the hyper-sensitive class); the eclipse recordings re-baselined at their noise floor (lunar per-century medians 0.1–0.5 min, centerlines 0.1–0.4″). Packages: @essrt/physics 11.2.0, @essrt/model-values 10.3.0.
_v16_1Note: v16.0 → v16.1 (2026-10, plan 06 I3): a MINOR — the Sun planetary completion's long-period rows re-derived, structure of the completion unchanged. (1) The Earth–Mars–Jupiter long inequality 4λ_E − 8λ_Ma + 3λ_J rides the planets' eccentricity vectors of date in D'Alembert form (a sum over Earth, Mars and Jupiter of e_X(t)·[a cos(θ + ϖ_X(t)) + b sin(θ + ϖ_X(t))], the embedded 1-kyr grid from the banked series), derived on the model's own N-body over ±20,000 yr — the constant row held inside ±3000 yr and drifted 3.7″ beyond. (2) The completion's carriers are the model's own banked J2000 sidereal mean motions (the planet records' rounded periods minus p₀ sat 4.1″/yr off for Venus). (3) The lunar equation's argument is the framework's Moon elongation of date (ṅ included). (4) The Venus–Earth row (fifth order, resonant — a cluster) stays constant, re-derived over ±3100 yr on the new carriers. Against DE441 in the fixed J2000 frame the per-millennium scatter at ±9000 yr fell from 4.1–4.7″ to 2.3–3.6″; against Horizons the modern window reads 0.83 ± 0.78″ (was 0.74 ± 0.94), the ancient millennia 4.16/3.85/2.89″ sd (was 4.44/3.81/2.82).
_v16Note: v15.0 → v16.0 (2026-09, owner: 'all calculations should match what we measure in the scene'): a structural MAJOR — three year-length laws restated so the scene's measured years reproduce them (the scene-sampled gate tools/verify/scene-year-lengths.js, 30 ms). (1) The tropical year of date is built on the equinox's GENERAL-PRECESSION rate (the broken angle through the node of the ecliptic of date — the literature's p_A, `generalPrecessionLonDeg`), not the projected J2000 longitude rate: equal at J2000, apart with the square of the ecliptic's tilt (0.05 s at ±4 kyr, ~1 s beyond 100 kyr; 5.9″ of Sun at −3000). (2) The year relations are rate-form with the sampler's Julian-year unit named — the precession period had been counted in tropical years by the pair's beat and realised per Julian year by the frame (26 ms of tropical year; periods are now quoted in Julian years, the J2000 reading 25,771.4 unchanged). (3) The anomalistic year and Earth's apsidal period ride the ONE movement's own apsidal line (the scene's perihelion), no longer the planet chain's secular tangent (3.3 s at 0 AD, 395 s at +25 kyr). With it the D6 λ̇ channel is re-banked as the least-squares quadratic slope of the run's unwrapped L over 10 kyr (the 2-kyr boxcar of step rates carried 0.1–0.3 s of node noise, +18…28″ of Sun by 6500 against DE441). Sun vs Horizons 3.66 → 2.57″ mean; against DE441 in the fixed J2000 frame rms 18.9 → 5.4″ over ±9000 yr; cardinal instants −1.49 → −1.04 min.
_v15Note: v14.0 → v15.0 (2026-09, plan 06 §9 item 10): a structural MAJOR — a new term family on the precession. THE PRECESSION OF DATE: the spin integration's precession constant is the secular (composed) law times two factors of date, both exactly 1 at J2000 — the solar torque's (1 − e²)^(−3/2) at the eccentricity OF DATE (the solar-share formula held e at J2000) and J₂(t)/J₂₀, the oblateness of date from the GIA channel (ψ̇ ∝ the dynamical ellipticity; scaled on the observed dJ₂/dt, the new input deepTime.j2RateJ2000PerYr, Cox & Chao 2002). Measured, theory against theory: the equinox of date against Vondrák et al. (2011) −27″ → −7″ at −3000 (≤ 0.3″ inside −500…+2500); the Sun against Horizons 9.4 → 3.7″ mean over ±3000 yr; the cardinal instants −3.8 → −1.5 min; the obliquity against La2004 over the last million years 80 → 14″ rms. Unchanged: the secular composed law and its deep-time gates, the unit H(t), the era clock, the tidal chain, the planet chains, the day, the polar moment, the eccentricity. The Sun's longitude of date follows the equinox and the Moon's arguments do not, so ancient eclipse geometry moves by the equinox correction (~8 km of umbra track at −135; the eclipse audit unchanged at its rounding). Also in this identity: the lunar-alignment campaign re-recorded (it had been stale since the deep-eccentricity slope anchor — its inputs block now lists what it runs on).
_v14Note: v13.0 → v14.0 (2026-09, plan 06 Phases 1–2 + D7): a structural MAJOR. (1) The climate formula's L1 is no longer a divisor set: 25 lines derived from the engine's own Earth z/ζ modes and p (relative amplitude ≥ 0.1) plus the g₂−g₅ fundamental and its two climate-internal harmonics, one home (data/l1-physical-lines.json); the 33-integer comb and the L2 layer retire (T1). (2) A new term family: α(t) is the LAGGED viscoelastic response of the polar moment to that ice history, α = α₀ − k·[L1 − ⟨L1⟩_τ], k derived at runtime from the Cox–Chao rate, τ = 6 kyr MEASURED by the historical ΔT record (D7) — the instantaneous α ∝ L1 law and its stored scale retire. (3) The Core-mantle swing ships as the two-impulse episode only; its drive tone retires at amplitude 0. (4) The ΔT stack refit and the whole historical gate suite re-baselined (lunar 1213 s / 119 of 267, solar 665 s / 43 of 89); the ΔT-stack lattice labels measured at chance level (T5) and stated in years. The tidal chain, the planet chains, the Moon chain and the cardinal clock are unchanged.
